record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Analyze the time-dependent spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills equations, analogously to the known analysis of the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar field equations.

artifact.status_search_result: The fully time-dependent spherically symmetric Einstein–Yang–Mills system has been studied in special cases (e.g., Bondi-coordinate formulations of the EYM–Higgs equations, global existence of certain homogeneous or small-data solutions, and numerical studies of critical collapse by Choptuik, Bizoń and others), but a complete rigorous analysis paralleling that achieved for the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar field system (Christodoulou's program: global well-posedness in BV, weak cosmic censorship, critical collapse) has not been carried out. The broad program therefore remains open, with only partial results available.

status_evidence.title: Global solutions, and their decay properties, of the spherically symmetric Einstein–Yang–Mills–Higgs equations
status_evidence.snippet: Global existence and uniqueness results established for initial data in specific Banach function spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Partial global-existence results exist for related EYM-Higgs systems but not a complete analogue of the Einstein-scalar field analysis.

status_evidence.title: On the spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs equations in Bondi coordinates
status_evidence.snippet: Characteristic Cauchy problem for the EYMH equations in Bondi coordinates.
status_evidence.claim: Time-dependent formulations have been studied in Bondi coordinates, indicating ongoing partial analysis.

status_evidence.title: Static spherically symmetric solutions of the Einstein–Yang–Mills equations
status_evidence.snippet: Most analytic work has focused on the static case.
status_evidence.claim: Most rigorous results concern the static reduction; the dynamical case is comparatively underdeveloped.
